dispositions.rationale: ACR-A25 claims only what it observes: the fixture is one set of bytes in both repositories at the release commits. The behaviour is observed elsewhere. ACR-A23 drives the production entry point, main(), over every fixture case, and ACR-A26 renders through the installed binary and parses the result. A production path that bypasses the parser fails one of those two.

The cross-reference is a maintenance aid stated in ACR-D5. The failure it guards against is the two copies drifting apart, and ACR-A21, ACR-A22 and ACR-A25 exclude that failure by holding both copies to one fixture. A criterion that inspects source text for a path would pin an artifact where the obligation is the shared reading.

ACR-D7 is a scope boundary on the change, and no behaviour depends on it. A change to prgroom's source cannot land unseen: the repository's version guard fails a prgroom source change that neither bumps the release nor marks it partial, and the change is visible in the diff under review.

No finite check establishes that no other verb ever writes the marker. ACR-D1 fixes the writers at two, and the marker's `[work]` prefix is the facade's reserved namespace. A third writer would be a new decision amending ACR-D1, and the attack would then face it.

This spec ships no consumer that writes a rendering. ACR-D3's sentence states the contract that the later slices' consumers inherit, and their own specs carry the criteria for it. The one consumer path in scope, parsing the live rendering, is ACR-A26.
The same hole as behavioural-outcome-4, rejected on the same ground: the drift the cross-reference guards against is excluded by ACR-A21, ACR-A22 and ACR-A25.
The same hole as behavioural-outcome-5, rejected on the same ground: ACR-D7 is a scope boundary, and a consumer source change is visible in the diff and to the version guard.

ACR-A38 states without qualification that an item whose last marker names another path keeps its notes, so a repoint through any option fails it. An option the interface does not have needs no criterion of its own.

No check that runs inside one repository can observe the other. ACR-A25 fixes the point at which the release is judged, which is what a verification child is for. A later edit to either copy is a new change that the fixture suites of ACR-A21 to ACR-A23 still gate in its own repository.

Verified in workcli: deliver reads its manifest from PATH before it reconciles, and its reader answers any unreadable path with a usage error. An empty PATH is unreadable, so deliver already refuses it before writing anything, and no marker can be recorded.

parts.statement: The exact marker names the spec; the last marker wins; absence of the marker means no named spec.
Non-marker notes and unrelated tracker metadata do not affect rendering.
Only `work acceptance set` and `work deliver --spec` write the named-spec marker.
Acceptance set resolves PATH from the working directory, records it relative to the repository root, permits outside paths in `..` form, and rejects an empty PATH without writing.
Changing only the named spec is an amendment subject to the started-work gate and trail; repeating unchanged text and path writes nothing.
Changing the spec path changes resolution, byte-identical repointing preserves output, and later spec-text edits appear without a tracker write.

obligations.source: ACR-D1: “The named spec is therefore a note marker, `[work] acceptance spec: <path>`... The payload of the item's last such marker is its named spec... Two verbs write the marker... No other note affects a rendering.”
obligations.statement: Items name specs through one append-only facade marker, and acceptance-set amendments preserve the specified marker and gate semantics.

parts.statement: Direct root and subdirectory renders use the checkout root, and a linked worktree whose `.git` is a file uses its own root.
Repository discovery resolves a symlinked working directory before searching its ancestors.
When multiple `.git` ancestors exist, repository discovery chooses the nearest one.
Absolute and lexically escaping paths are refused; lexically internal paths proceed.
A symlink escaping the resolved root is refused, while an internal symlink is followed.
A spec-naming item without a repository root is refused, while an item naming no spec needs no root.

obligations.source: ACR-D2: “The repository root is the nearest ancestor of the resolved working directory holding a `.git` entry... In a linked worktree it is that worktree's root... A symlink whose target stays inside the root is followed. A symlink whose target lies outside is refused.”
obligations.statement: Named specs resolve reproducibly within the current repository root, including linked-worktree and symlink boundaries.

parts.statement: The envelope data is exactly `{id, markdown}`, and markdown has the specified headings, blank lines, quoted description, criterion bullets, LF endings, and no extra material.
Descriptions containing criterion-shaped text, headings, fences, blank lines, and CRLF breaks round-trip as quoted description rather than criteria.
Description lines follow the complete line-boundary behavior of Python's `str.splitlines`, not only LF and CRLF.
Non-ASCII markdown content is preserved in its UTF-8 representation.
A rendering consumer writes M's UTF-8 bytes verbatim.
Title, labels, priority, status, and unrelated notes do not enter the rendering.

obligations.source: ACR-D3: “`work acceptance render ID` answers in the facade's JSON envelope... The rendering is the UTF-8 encoding of M, and a consumer writes those bytes verbatim... Lines split as Python's `str.splitlines` splits them... M holds nothing else.”
obligations.statement: Successful rendering has the exact JSON payload, markdown layout, line handling, and byte representation specified by ACR-D3.

parts.statement: Blank field lines are ignored, equivalent citation layouts resolve equally, and citations retain field order.
Only a whole citation line on an item naming a spec is a citation; all other lines, including lines on unnamed items, are text.
An explicit criterion line preserves its valid ID and text.
Other text lines receive the exact normalized P-Tn ID and stripped text, including the `ITEM` fallback.
Resolved criterion text is not reinterpreted as citations, and an empty cited entry contributes no bullet.

obligations.source: ACR-D4: “Each nonblank line of the field is one unit... On an item naming a spec, a citation line matches... On an item naming no spec, every line is a text line... Any other text line renders as `- **P-Tn**`...”
obligations.statement: The acceptance field is classified line by line into citations and text, with stable explicit or generated IDs.

parts.statement: The fixture-represented heading scope, continuation, entry-opening, fence, empty-entry, and ordering rules produce the expected entries in both parsers.
A heading is in scope when its text contains the phrase `acceptance criteria`, even when other heading text surrounds that phrase.
Spec-lint returns empty and repeated entries in document order.
Empty entries define no criterion, need no evidence, and do not change existing lint results for text-bearing entries.
A citation resolves only to one defining entry; missing and repeated definitions are refused, while one empty definition contributes nothing.
Each parser module's source names the path of its counterpart.

obligations.source: ACR-D5: “Its scope is every heading whose text contains `acceptance criteria`, case-insensitively... Each following line joins the entry... Spec-lint exposes `parse_criteria_entries(text)`... Workcli carries a counterpart module. Each copy's source names the other's path.”
obligations.statement: Spec-lint and workcli share the widened entry grammar and agree on ordered entries, empty entries, repetition, and citation resolution.

parts.statement: Missing, unreadable, non-UTF-8, unresolved, ambiguous, path, notes, and root failures return their specified E_RENDER cause and details; unknown items retain E_NOT_FOUND.
Every duplicate pairing, repeated citation, and empty-entry duplicate is refused with duplicate-id and the offending ID.
When several failures apply, path, file, and field-unit checks select the first failure in the specified order.
Successful and refused renders make no mutating backend call and write no file.
Repeated renders of equal refused input return the same complete refusal.

obligations.source: ACR-D6: “A refused rendering returns error code `E_RENDER`... `detail.cause` comes from a closed vocabulary... Checks run in the table's order... The first failure is the one reported, so equal input always gets the same refusal... Rendering never writes.”
obligations.statement: Rendering failures use the closed E_RENDER cause vocabulary, report the appropriate offending fields, choose failures deterministically, and never mutate state.

parts.statement: Spec-lint and prgroom recover exactly the rendered acceptance entries even when quoted descriptions contain parser-shaped text.
Prgroom remains unchanged, and review-panel and ac-attack do not gain entry-parsing logic; only spec-lint's existing grammar changes.

obligations.source: ACR-D7: “Only spec-lint's grammar changes. The verdict poster is unchanged... The review-panel and ac-attack emitters parse no entries.”
obligations.statement: Existing consumers retain their parser boundaries while remaining compatible with rendered output.

parts.statement: Delivery marks each reconciled or minted unmarked item with the root-relative path, including outside-root paths and invocations from subdirectories.
Replays write at most one marker per item, repair a mint-to-marker interruption, and leave completed reconciliations unchanged.
An item already naming another spec is not repointed and is identified in the reply.
When several items name other specs, the reply lists every one of them.
`work deliver --spec` does not accept a `--why` option.
Every delivered item's acceptance field retains its manifest AC text byte for byte.
Manifest ID lists become citations, while trailing punctuation and prose remain text.

obligations.source: ACR-D8: “Reconciling a placeholder, `work deliver --spec PATH` writes the ACR-D1 marker... it also marks every manifest child... Deliver never repoints... its reply lists each item whose last marker names another path. Deliver takes no `--why`... Each item keeps its manifest AC text.”
obligations.statement: Spec delivery marks every applicable placeholder and child without repointing, preserves manifest text, recovers interrupted work, and reports conflicts.

parts.statement: Both parser implementations and the renderer produce the fixture's expected entries, golden bytes, and refusals.
For every fixture rule F1 through F14, a deliberately violating parser or renderer variant is caught by a case tagged with that rule.
At the commits delivering Slices A through C, the fixture copies are byte-identical and both suites pass.
The agents-config fixture and workcli's vendored copy remain byte-identical in the delivered state, not only at the Slice A-to-C checkpoints.
After human installation, the live work command renders an item citing this spec and spec-lint recovers the cited nonempty entries in order.

obligations.source: ACR-D9: “The fixture lives in agents-config... Workcli vendors a byte-identical copy... `cases.json` lists each case... `entries.json` lists the entries expected... The rules are F1–F14.” Also: “Slice E: cross-repository verification.”
obligations.statement: The two repositories share a fixture that exercises F1 through F14, detects violations, and proves parser and installed-renderer interoperability.

ground.reason: ACR-A24 promises that each fixture rule detects a renderer or parser variant violating that rule. Its check requires only that each variant fail a case tagged with the rule. It does not require an isolated mutation or establish that the tagged rule caused the failure, so an unrelated crash can satisfy the check.

objections.objection: The mutation check can credit a fixture rule for a failure caused by an unrelated defect.
objections.obligation: Each fixture rule must distinguish an implementation that violates that rule from one that preserves it.

scenario.expect: The tagged case fails and ACR-A24 passes, while the fixture has not demonstrated that it detects the targeted rule violation.
scenario.given: A variant violates F12 but also introduces an import-time error, and its listed F12-tagged case fails before exercising symlink handling.
scenario.when: The Workcli suite runs the ACR-A24 check.

ground.reason: The traceability table says ACR-A25 verifies the parent rendering and parser outcomes, but ACR-A25 and its check observe only byte-identical fixture files and green suites. Byte identity is valid for the fixture deliverable, but suite success is evidence rather than the promised runtime behaviour.

objections.objection: Identical fixtures and passing suites can discharge cross-repository behavioural obligations without directly observing those obligations.
objections.obligation: The delivered implementations in both repositories must exhibit the parent rendering, parsing and empty-entry behaviours.

scenario.expect: Fixture digests match and both suites pass, so ACR-A25 passes, while a production parser path still violates a parent behaviour that the suites do not exercise.
scenario.given: Both repositories contain identical fixtures and their selected fixture tests pass, but one production entry point bypasses the parser exercised by those tests.
scenario.when: The ACR-A25 verification row compares digests and records the two suite results.

ground.reason: ACR-A29 combines entry parsing, document-level definition, slice-reference failure and evidence-row exemption. Its named check observes parsed entries, the slice failure and unchanged corpus lint results, but it never sets up an otherwise-valid empty entry without an evidence row and asserts that no evidence error occurs.

objections.objection: The evidence-row exemption can be absent while every observation named for ACR-A29 passes.
objections.obligation: An empty criterion entry must not require an evidence row.

scenario.expect: The named ACR-A29 observations pass, while spec-lint still reports a missing-evidence error for the empty entry.
scenario.given: The parser returns empty text correctly and a slice citing only that entry fails as required, but the evidence validator treats the empty entry as requiring a row.
scenario.when: The suites run the checks listed for ACR-A21 and ACR-A27 through ACR-A29.

ground.reason: ACR-D5 promises that each grammar copy's source names the other copy's path. No acceptance criterion or check inspects either source for that cross-reference.

objections.objection: Both grammar implementations can pass every parser and fixture check while omitting the required maintenance cross-reference.
objections.obligation: Each counterpart grammar source must name the other source path.

scenario.expect: All named checks pass, while neither source names its counterpart.
scenario.given: The two grammar implementations return every expected fixture entry but contain no reference to one another.
scenario.when: The acceptance checks run.

ground.reason: ACR-D7 promises that prgroom's verdict poster and source remain unchanged. The document checks prgroom output on golden renderings and says its existing tests pass unchanged, but names no source-diff check. Equivalent or compensating source changes can satisfy both observations.

objections.objection: The implementation can modify prgroom despite the explicit no-change decision and still pass every named check.
objections.obligation: The change must not modify prgroom's source or require its release and reinstall.

scenario.expect: Golden-rendering comparisons and existing tests pass, while the promised unchanged prgroom source is absent.
scenario.given: Prgroom's parser is modified without changing its observed golden-rendering results.
scenario.when: The agents-config suites run the checks named for ACR-A27.

ground.reason: The checks exercise marker writes through acceptance set and deliver, but none observes whether another verb can write the reserved marker.

objections.objection: A third verb may write or alter the named-spec marker while every criterion still passes.

scenario.expect: Every listed check passes, but the unrelated verb appends a named-spec marker and changes the spec used by later renders.
scenario.given: An implementation in which an unrelated update verb also writes `[work] acceptance spec:` notes
scenario.when: The listed checks run without invoking that update verb

ground.reason: The root checks use direct root and subdirectory paths. They do not enter the checkout through a symlinked working directory.

objections.objection: Repository discovery may inspect the lexical working-directory path instead of resolving it first.

scenario.expect: Every listed check passes, but rendering is refused with `no-repository-root` instead of using the checkout reached through the symlink.
scenario.given: A symlink outside the checkout that points to a directory inside it, and an implementation that searches the symlink's lexical ancestors
scenario.when: A spec-naming item is rendered with that symlinked directory as the working directory

ground.reason: No check places the working directory beneath two repository roots and observes which `.git` ancestor wins.

objections.objection: Repository discovery may select an outer repository instead of the nearest repository ancestor.

scenario.expect: Every listed check passes, but the spec is resolved against the outer repository rather than the nearest nested repository.
scenario.given: A checkout nested inside another checkout and an implementation that selects the outermost `.git` ancestor
scenario.when: A relative named spec is rendered from the nested checkout

ground.reason: The description check covers CRLF and several syntactic shapes, but not the other line boundaries recognized by Python's `str.splitlines`.

objections.objection: Description rendering may implement only CR, LF, and CRLF splitting while violating the specified `str.splitlines` semantics.

scenario.expect: Every listed check passes, but the two logical description lines appear as one quoted line.
scenario.given: A passing renderer that splits descriptions only on CR and LF, and a description containing a Unicode line separator
scenario.when: The item is rendered

ground.reason: No named fixture rule or check requires non-ASCII description or criterion text to be emitted as its UTF-8 bytes.

objections.objection: The renderer may mishandle non-ASCII text while passing all ASCII fixture cases.

scenario.expect: Every listed check passes, but the rendered markdown escapes, replaces, or mis-encodes the non-ASCII characters instead of preserving their UTF-8 representation.
scenario.given: A renderer that passes the listed fixtures but applies an ASCII-only output conversion
scenario.when: An item containing non-ASCII description or criterion text is rendered

ground.reason: The checks compare the renderer's envelope and exercise parsers, but none observes a consumer writing the returned markdown bytes.

objections.objection: A consumer may normalize or decorate the markdown instead of writing the rendering verbatim.

scenario.expect: Every renderer and parser check passes, but the consumer-produced artifact has changed line endings or added surrounding text.
scenario.given: A conforming renderer and a consumer that rewrites its markdown before saving it
scenario.when: The consumer writes a successful rendering

ground.reason: Fixture rule F14 checks heading case and the closing heading level, but no stated scenario uses a heading whose text contains additional words around `acceptance criteria`.

objections.objection: The parsers may require the heading text to equal `Acceptance criteria` instead of merely containing that phrase.

scenario.expect: Every listed check passes, but the parser returns no entries from that section.
scenario.given: A parser that accepts only an exact case-insensitive heading and a document headed `## Draft acceptance criteria for S1`
scenario.when: The document is passed to either criteria parser

ground.reason: The parser checks observe returned entries. They do not inspect either module's source for the required reference to its counterpart.

objections.objection: The two parser copies may omit the required source-level cross-reference while remaining behaviorally identical.

scenario.expect: Every parser and fixture check passes, but neither source file names the other file's path.
scenario.given: Two behaviorally conforming parser modules with the counterpart-path references removed
scenario.when: The full acceptance suite runs

ground.reason: Refusal cases are checked individually, but no check renders the same refused input twice and compares the complete refusal envelopes.

objections.objection: Equal refused inputs may produce different first failures on successive renders.

scenario.expect: Every listed check passes, but two renders of the same invalid item return different causes or offending fields.
scenario.given: An implementation that alternates between two applicable refusal causes while remaining non-mutating
scenario.when: The same invalid item is rendered twice without any intervening change

ground.reason: The compatibility check observes parser output, but no criterion checks that prgroom, review-panel, and ac-attack source remain outside the grammar change.

objections.objection: Existing consumer source may be changed even though the design promises that only spec-lint's grammar changes.

scenario.expect: Every behavior and fixture check passes, but prgroom or an emitter now contains new entry-parsing logic.
scenario.given: A change that modifies existing consumer parsers while preserving their tested outputs
scenario.when: The acceptance suites and source-independent checks run

ground.reason: The delivery setup contains one item naming another spec. It does not check a reconciliation containing two or more differently named items.

objections.objection: Delivery may report only the first item it refuses to repoint instead of listing every such item.

scenario.expect: Every listed check passes, but the reply lists only one of the two mismatched item IDs.
scenario.given: A manifest reconciliation with two children whose last markers name different specs, and an implementation that stops collecting IDs after the first
scenario.when: The placeholder is reconciled with `work deliver --spec PATH`

ground.reason: No check invokes deliver with `--why` and requires the option to be rejected.

objections.objection: `work deliver --spec` may accept `--why`, contrary to the specified interface and its amendment-gate rationale.

scenario.expect: Every listed check passes, but deliver accepts `--why` and repoints the item.
scenario.given: An implementation that adds a `--why` option to deliver and uses it to permit repointing
scenario.when: A user reconciles an already named item with `work deliver --spec OTHER --why reason`

ground.reason: The digest check is tied to the commits delivering Slices A through C. No criterion requires the copies to remain identical in the final state or after Slice D.

objections.objection: The vendored fixture may diverge after its historical equality evidence is recorded.

scenario.expect: All criteria, including the historical ACR-A25 evidence, remain satisfied, but the two repositories finish with different fixture bytes.
scenario.given: Matching fixtures at the Slice A-to-C verification commits followed by a Slice D change to only workcli's vendored fixture
scenario.when: The final delivered state is evaluated

ground.reason: ACR-A31's closing sentence grants a render to any relative path whose lexical normalization stays inside the root, while ACR-A32 refuses a path that resolves through a symlink to outside the root. A lexically-inside path containing an escaping symlink satisfies both, and the two criteria demand opposite verdicts for the same rendering.

objections.objection: The criteria let an implementation pass ACR-A31 by rendering a lexically-inside path while failing ACR-A32's symlink refusal, or pass ACR-A32 by refusing while failing ACR-A31's unconditional 'renders'. ACR-A31 needs to carve out the symlink case (render only when the resolved path also stays inside the root).

scenario.expect: ACR-A31 requires a successful render because the lexical normalization of 'link/spec.md' stays inside the root; ACR-A32 requires refusal with E_RENDER and cause spec-path-escapes because the path resolves through a symlink outside the resolved root
scenario.given: An item whose recorded spec path is 'link/spec.md', where 'link' is a symlink inside the repository root pointing to a directory outside the root that holds a readable, valid UTF-8 spec file
scenario.when: work acceptance render runs on that item from inside the checkout

ground.reason: ACR-A7 says an explicit-ID text line renders with 'that text unchanged', while ACR-D4 specifies whitespace stripping only for generated-ID lines and never states whether the text portion of an explicit-ID line is stripped. The decision the wording leaves open is whether leading and trailing whitespace around the text of a '- **ID** text' line survives into the rendering, and each reading produces different bytes.

objections.objection: The criteria admit two renderers that disagree byte for byte on explicit-ID lines carrying extra whitespace: one preserving the text exactly as written after the ID, one stripping it like generated-ID lines. ACR-A13's byte-for-byte requirement then pins different golden outputs depending on which reading the fixture author took.

scenario.expect: Under ACR-A7's 'unchanged' reading the bullet is '- **AC1**   the system shall render   ' with the original spacing; under the stripped reading the bullet is '- **AC1** the system shall render', and the criteria do not say which is correct
scenario.given: An item naming no spec whose acceptance field holds the line '- **AC1**   the system shall render   ' with multiple inner leading spaces and trailing spaces after the text
scenario.when: work acceptance render produces the criterion bullet for that line

ground.reason: ACR-D1 names the empty-PATH usage error for `acceptance set` only, and ACR-A37 pins it only for that verb, while `work deliver --spec PATH` takes the same PATH argument under the same decision. No criterion states deliver's behavior on an empty PATH, so the criteria admit an implementation that records an empty marker or silently resolves the empty string to the working directory.

objections.objection: An empty PATH passed to `work deliver --spec` has no specified outcome: no refusal, no usage error, and no defined marker payload, even though the sibling verb's identical input is pinned as a usage error naming `--spec` that writes nothing.

scenario.expect: A usage error naming `--spec`, with no marker written and no reconciliation performed, matching the set verb's empty-PATH rule
scenario.given: A manifest placeholder ready to reconcile, on the fake backend
scenario.when: `work deliver --spec ""` runs

ground.reason: Notes are append-only user-visible text, so a note matching the marker prefix with an empty or whitespace-only payload can exist on an item. ACR-D1 makes the last such marker the named spec, ACR-D6's closed cause vocabulary has no cause for an empty recorded path, and ACR-A37 refuses empty PATH only at set time. Render's behavior for this state is neither covered nor ruled out.

objections.objection: An item whose last `[work] acceptance spec:` marker carries an empty or whitespace-only payload has no defined rendering outcome: the refusal table has no cause for it, and the criteria say nothing about whether render refuses, renders without a spec, or errors differently.

scenario.expect: A defined outcome, presumably an `E_RENDER` refusal with a named cause, since the item names a spec whose path cannot be resolved
scenario.given: An item whose notes contain `[work] acceptance spec:` followed by no path, appended by hand or by a tool other than the two marker-writing verbs
scenario.when: `work acceptance render ID` runs
